steps.title: A family
steps.body: Muscat is a family of over 200 grapes. The finest is Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, small-berried, used in Asti, Alsace, Beaumes-de-Venise and Rutherglen. Muscat of Alexandria, larger-berried and less refined, grows in Spain, Portugal's Setúbal, Sicily as Zibibbo, and Chile. Muscat Ottonel, lighter, grows in Alsace and Austria. Some Muscats are pink or black.

steps.title: Ancient roots
steps.body: Muscat is among the oldest grapes, probably from Greece or the eastern Mediterranean; the Greeks and Romans spread it. Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains is thought to be the oldest; Muscat of Alexandria is its offspring with a table grape. It grows in Greece, as Moschato on Samos, and across the Mediterranean.

steps.prompt: Match each Muscat to its region.
steps.explanation: The Muscat family spreads around the Mediterranean.

steps.body: Zibibbo, Sicily's name for Muscat of Alexandria, makes the famous Passito di Pantelleria from sun-dried grapes on a volcanic island south of Sicily.

steps.prompt: Which Muscat is considered the finest?
steps.explanation: Its small berries give the most refined wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Muscat is a family of over 200 grapes
Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains is the finest
It spread from Greece across the Mediterranean
